title: Design a Proximity Service (Yelp / Google Maps Nearby)
subtitle: Geohashing, Spatial Quadtrees, and Redis Geospatial indexing for sub-10ms location searches

stages.title: Stage 1 — SQL Spatial Query (Bounding Box / Haversine)
stages.bottleneck: Executing `WHERE latitude BETWEEN x1 AND x2 AND longitude BETWEEN y1 AND y2` scans millions of rows; 2D spatial indexing is slow on relational DBs.
stages.narrative: **Relational Spatial Query.** Calculates Haversine distance between user coordinates and every restaurant in the database table.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Geohash Grid Indexing in Redis
stages.bottleneck: Geohash boundary precision issues (two places 50m apart across a grid border have completely different prefix strings).
stages.narrative:
**Geohashing Grid Index.** Encodes 2D coordinates into a Base32 1D string (e.g. `9q9hv`).

**8 Neighbor Check:** To prevent grid border misses, the search queries the center Geohash plus all 8 adjacent neighbor grid cells.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Spatial Quadtree Memory Index & CDN Edge Caching
stages.bottleneck: Static business location data changes rarely, but queries spike constantly.
stages.narrative: **Quadtrees & Edge Tile Caching.** A Quadtree recursively subdivides 2D space into 4 quadrants until each node contains ≤ 100 places. Map tiles are pre-rendered and cached at CDN edge locations.
